title: Veridian brick manifest
description: Parsed from veridian.toml at the root of a brick directory. Declares identity, how to spawn the brick, what contracts it implements, and what capabilities it needs.

isolation.description: How the kernel spawns this brick and what it may reach from inside. Absent (or mode = "process") is the Milestone 1 behaviour: a plain subprocess, the capability model enforced only at the host-service boundary and at spawn. mode = "container" runs the brick inside a Docker/Podman container the kernel controls, where `network = false` is an OS-level egress deny and `allow_hosts` is the only way out.

mode.description: "process" (default) spawns a plain subprocess. "container" spawns the brick inside a container via `docker run` / `podman run`, mounting the workspace read-write and the brick directory read-only.

image.description: Container image reference. Required when mode = "container". Must already carry whatever the brick's spawn command needs (interpreter, SDK); per-brick [dependencies] are not installed into it.

engine.description: Container engine. Omit to auto-detect (docker, then podman).

network.description: Egress switch, enforced at the container boundary (mode = "container" only). false (default) is `--network none`: the brick cannot open a socket to anything. true with a non-empty allow_hosts permits only those destinations; true with an empty allow_hosts grants unrestricted egress and is refused for any brick that also touches conversation content.

allow_hosts.description: Egress allowlist: "host" or "host:port" entries this brick may reach when network = true. Everything else is refused at the container boundary. This is the list `veridian stack show` enumerates so a stack's whole network surface is auditable from the manifests alone.

dependencies.description: Third-party packages this brick needs at runtime. When present, the brick is resolved into its own isolated environment on install (a private venv for python, a local node_modules for node) instead of sharing the kernel's interpreter. Bricks with no dependencies table keep running under ${python} / ${node} as before.

python.description: PEP 508 requirement strings, resolved with uv into a private venv.

node.description: package name -> semver range, written to a generated package.json and installed with npm into a local node_modules.
